title: Catch and file the links shared in your group chats
summary: KevinChu1110's driftnet takes links dropped in chats, finds the actual tool behind each post, summarises and files it; the author says five reels cost $0.00029 to judge.
agent_role: The AI reads each shared post, looks up the projects it names, writes a short summary and suggests a folder; the human approves filing and any tidy-up plan.
outcome: Author reports a real run where a Facebook reel with no links was turned into two correct project cards, and five reels were judged for $0.00029 in total.
what_they_did: The author built driftnet, which runs on your own computer. You drop links into a chat bot or click a browser button. It follows the post to the project it is really about, writes a short summary and files it in your folders. Suggested folders wait in an inbox for you to confirm.
how_it_went: The author shows a Facebook reel with no links going in; driftnet read the caption, found both projects on GitHub by name and filed each as a card. They say five reels cost $0.00029 to process.
worth_knowing: Links an AI model makes up are thrown away, and pages are cut to a short outline before any model sees them to keep costs tiny.
prompt: Help me set up a personal link catcher. Whenever I paste a link or a post into [chat app or a text file], open it, work out which tool, project or article it is really about, and look it up by exact name if no link is given. Write a two-line summary of what it is and why it might matter to me. Suggest one of my folders: [list your folders]. Save each item to [a spreadsheet or notes folder]. Never invent links. Show me the suggested filing for each batch and wait for my approval before saving.

curation.rationale: A working open-source pipeline with a real example of an AI reading a link-less video caption, finding the right projects and filing them; mostly a feature list, but concrete and reproducible.
